An independent high-precision recomputation reproduces the representative values within the explicitly float64 finite-box scope.
first_audit.claim_scope: Float64 finite-box evaluation at x=2 and 0<=p,q<=4 of the stipulated SU(3) Haar character integrals and normalized rho values, including the disclosed cross-route and refinement checks, without a physical Wilson-environment or plaquette identification.
first_audit.load_bearing_step: The stipulated coefficients at x=2 are evaluated independently by the Bessel-determinant sum and wall-stable Weyl-torus quadrature, which agree for all 25 weights within the disclosed tolerances.
first_audit.verdict_rationale: The runner computes rather than hard-codes the table: it evaluates the determinant-Bessel series and an independently implemented Weyl-torus quadrature, then checks refinement, normalization, symmetry, positivity, and hostile mutations. Independent reconstruction confirms the Haar factor, determinant indexing, and representative numerical values. The chain therefore closes within the stated float64 finite-box scope; a platform-independent enclosure and any physical environment or plaquette interpretation are expressly outside the claim.

second_audit.chain_closure_explanation: The completed runner reproduces the disclosed float64 table, but refinement drift and cross-route agreement do not certify the printed approximations to the underlying integrals. A rigorous truncation and quadrature enclosure remains missing.
second_audit.claim_scope: Finite-box evaluation at x=2 and 0<=p,q<=4 of the stipulated SU(3) Haar character integrals and normalized rho values, without any physical Wilson-environment or plaquette identification.
second_audit.load_bearing_step: The runner evaluates all 25 weights by two separately implemented routes and reports mutually agreeing values in the disclosed float64 run.
second_audit.notes_for_re_audit_if_any: other: add rigorous Bessel-tail bounds and certified quadrature or interval enclosures for all 25 coefficients, or explicitly retitle and scope the row as a platform-specific reproducibility certificate.
second_audit.verdict_rationale: The runner genuinely computes the 25 coefficients through a truncated Bessel-determinant sum and separately implemented Weyl-torus quadrature; it neither imports an expected table nor hard-codes the contested values. All twelve disclosed checks pass with the reported cross-errors and refinement drifts. However, the note expressly characterizes its tolerances as acceptance thresholds rather than analytic error bounds, so the evidence supports a reproducible float64 certificate but not theorem-grade certification of the underlying integral values to the printed precision.
